$comment: Generated by npm run registry:write from secrets/manifest/*.json. Edit those, not this file.

entries.name: INSTANCE_NAME
entries.description: Display name of the business this instance serves.
howToGet: Use the business's public name.

entries.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
entries.description: Permanent id of the business. Every row in the database is tagged with it.
howToGet: Lowercase the business name and replace spaces with dashes. Never change it after the first deploy.

entries.name: ENABLED_INTEGRATIONS
entries.description: Comma-separated catalog ids of the integrations this instance uses. Secrets for an integration are only required once it is listed here, and each built connector listed syncs on a schedule.
howToGet: Start empty and add each integration as you connect it.

entries.name: SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES
entries.description: Minutes between the end of one sync round and the start of the next, for every connector listed in ENABLED_INTEGRATIONS.
howToGet: Leave empty for 60. Use 5 to 1440.

entries.name: INSTANCE_API_KEY
entries.description: Key that agents and connectors send to call this instance's API.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.

entries.name: WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET
entries.description: Signs and verifies webhooks this instance sends or receives.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.

entries.name: SUPABASE_URL
entries.description: Address of this client's own Supabase project.
howToGet: Open supabase.com/dashboard and pick this client's project (each client gets its own).
Go to Project Settings > API.
Copy the Project URL.

entries.name: SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
entries.description: Public (anon or publishable) key for the same Supabase project.
howToGet: In the same Supabase project, go to Project Settings > API.
Copy the anon public key (or the publishable key).
It must come from the same project as SUPABASE_URL, or Supabase answers HTTP 401.

entries.name: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
entries.description: Server-only key that bypasses row-level security. Never put it in a browser or app.
howToGet: In the same Supabase project, go to Project Settings > API and copy the service_role (or secret) key.

entries.name: SUPABASE_DB_URL
entries.description: Direct Postgres connection string. The instance uses it to store data and run migrations.
howToGet: In the same Supabase project, click Connect at the top of the dashboard.
Copy the URI connection string (Session pooler works everywhere).
Replace [YOUR-PASSWORD] with the database password you set when creating the project.

entries.name: DOC_REGISTRY_IDS
entries.description: Comma-separated ids of the source-of-truth docs reasoning must consult. Optional, but without it every recommendation is marked degraded.
howToGet: Leave as is unless you maintain your own documentation registry.

entries.name: ENABLED_WRITES
entries.description: Comma-separated writes to outside systems this instance allows. Empty keeps every integration read-only.
howToGet: Leave empty. Every integration starts read-only.
Only after the client agrees in writing, list the exact actions, e.g. shopify:adjust_inventory, or shopify:* for every Shopify action.

entries.name: ENABLED_DEPARTMENTS
entries.description: Comma-separated retail departments this instance runs. Empty runs all of them.
howToGet: Leave empty to run every retail department.
To start smaller, list only the ids from docs/departments/README.md that the store uses.

entries.name: RAW_RETENTION_DAYS
entries.description: Days raw vendor data is kept before it is cleared. Facts, signals and links back to the source stay.
howToGet: Leave empty to keep 30 days.
Set a whole number from 1 to 365 if the client's policy asks for a different window.

entries.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: OAuth client for Gmail and Google Drive access.
howToGet: In console.cloud.google.com, create a project, enable the Gmail and Drive APIs, and create an OAuth client ID (Web application).

entries.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: Secret for the Google OAuth client.
howToGet: Shown next to the OAuth client ID in Google Cloud Console > APIs & Services > Credentials.

entries.name: GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI
entries.description: Where Google sends the owner back after granting access.
howToGet: Use https://<instance-host>/oauth/google/callback and add it to the OAuth client's authorized redirect URIs.

entries.name: CUSTOMER_REF_KEY
entries.description: Key for customer references: a keyed hash (HMAC-SHA256) of a customer's id in a system, email address or phone number, so one customer's records link up across systems without the id or any contact detail being stored. Changing it breaks those links, so it is never rotated.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup. Keep a copy in the password manager: losing it means a customer's earlier records no longer link to new ones.

entries.name: CORRESPONDENT_HASH_KEY
entries.description: The instance's own key for turning people's identifiers (email addresses, Slack user ids) into private references (HMAC-SHA256), so the brain can tell that two messages or appointments involve the same person without keeping who they are. Without the key, a reference can't be matched against a guessed identifier.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.
Don't rotate it unless a leak is suspected: a new key gives every person a new reference, so earlier history no longer lines up with later messages and appointments.

entries.name: AFFIRM_PUBLIC_API_KEY
entries.description: The merchant's Affirm public API key, sent with the private key as HTTP Basic auth to read transactions, disputes and settlements.
howToGet: An Affirm merchant administrator opens API keys in the Affirm merchant portal (www.affirm.com/dashboard/apikeys for a live account, sandbox.affirm.com/dashboard/apikeys for the sandbox one).
Copy the public API key straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: AFFIRM_PRIVATE_API_KEY
entries.description: The merchant's Affirm private API key. Affirm can't limit a key to reading, so this one could also capture, refund and void loans; the connector only ever sends its listed GET reads.
howToGet: On the same API keys page, copy the private API key straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
Use the sandbox page's keys with AFFIRM_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox and the live page's keys with production; each environment has its own pair.

entries.name: AFFIRM_MERCHANT_ID
entries.description: The Affirm Merchant ID, which Affirm's settlement reads require. Not a secret, but it names the merchant's account.
howToGet: Ask Affirm merchant support (the Support widget in the merchant portal) for the account's Merchant ID as the settlements API takes it, and copy it here.

entries.name: AFFIRM_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which Affirm host the keys are for: sandbox (sandbox.affirm.com) or production (api.affirm.com). There is no default, so a sandbox setting can't reach a live account by accident and the other way round. Canadian accounts on Affirm's global hosts aren't supported yet.
howToGet: Use sandbox with the keys from sandbox.affirm.com/dashboard/apikeys and production with the live keys.

entries.name: AFFIRM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: The signing secret Affirm signs webhooks with (Affirm-Signature, HMAC-SHA512). Affirm's docs say it is the merchant's private API key unless Affirm set up another. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: Affirm sets webhooks and their signature up itself: ask through the Support widget in the merchant portal, and ask which secret signs them.
Copy that secret straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
entries.description: Lets Brain A use Claude for reasoning.
howToGet: Go to console.anthropic.com > API Keys and create a key named after this instance.

entries.name: AUTHORIZE_NET_API_LOGIN_ID
entries.description: The merchant's Authorize.net API Login ID, used with the Transaction Key to read transaction reports.
howToGet: In the Authorize.net Merchant Interface, go to Account > Settings > Security Settings > API Credentials and Keys.
Copy the API Login ID straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: AUTHORIZE_NET_TRANSACTION_KEY
entries.description: The merchant's Authorize.net Transaction Key. Authorize.net can't limit a key to reading, so this one could also charge, refund and void; the connector only ever sends reporting requests.
howToGet: On the same API Credentials and Keys page, create a new Transaction Key. Leave Disable Old Key unticked if another system still uses the current one.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store. Authorize.net shows it once. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
Under Account > Settings > Security Settings > Transaction Details API, make sure the Transaction Details API is turned on; the connector reads through it.

entries.name: AUTHORIZE_NET_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which Authorize.net endpoint the account is on: sandbox for a developer sandbox account, production for a merchant's live one. There is no default, so a sandbox setting can't reach a live account by accident and the other way round.
howToGet: Use sandbox with keys from a sandbox account made at developer.authorize.net, and production with the merchant's live keys.

entries.name: AUTHORIZE_NET_SIGNATURE_KEY
entries.description: The Signature Key Authorize.net signs webhooks with (X-ANET-Signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: On the API Credentials and Keys page, create a new Signature Key and copy it straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: BANK_STATEMENTS_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder of statement exports, with one subfolder per account named for its type and last four digits, such as checking-1234 or card-5678. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.
Inside it, make one folder per account, named like checking-1234, savings-2345 or card-5678.
Download each account's activity as CSV from online banking into its folder.

entries.name: BANK_STATEMENTS_PROFILES
entries.description: Which columns each bank's exports use: generic, or the path to a JSON file in the client's private instance repo mapping account folders to parsing profiles.
howToGet: Leave as generic when the exports have Date, Description and Amount (or Debit and Credit) columns.
Otherwise write the profiles in the client's private instance repo and put the file's path here.

entries.name: BIGCOMMERCE_STORE_HASH
entries.description: The BigCommerce store's hash, the short ID in its API path (api.bigcommerce.com/stores/<hash>/). Not a secret. The connector checks that the token belongs to this store before reading anything.
howToGet: It is shown as the API path when the store-level API account is created (Settings > Store-level API accounts), between /stores/ and /v3/.
It also appears in the store's control panel address: store-<hash>.mybigcommerce.com.

entries.name: BIGCOMMERCE_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: Access token of a store-level API account holding read-only scopes. BigCommerce can't report a token's scopes, so give it nothing but read-only scopes; the connector also sends only GET requests to its listed paths.
howToGet: In the BigCommerce control panel open Settings > Store-level API accounts > Create API account, type V2/V3 API token, named KaratOS.
Set these scopes to read-only and leave every other scope at None: Orders, Products (which covers price lists), Customers, Information & settings, Store inventory. Never choose modify.
Save, then copy the Access token straight into the host's secret store. BigCommerce shows it once; never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: BIGCOMMERCE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: Shared secret BigCommerce sends in the x-karatos-webhook-secret header of each webhook, set as a custom header when the webhook is created, since store webhooks carry no signature. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.
Create each webhook (POST /v3/hooks) with headers {"x-karatos-webhook-secret": <this value>}.

entries.name: CHASE_IMPORT_MODE
entries.description: How Chase data arrives: CSV exports, PDF statements, or both. The client chooses.
howToGet: Ask the client how they want to send statements.
Use manual_csv for CSV exports, manual_pdf for PDF statements, or manual_csv_and_pdf for both (for example CSV for recent activity and PDFs for older years).

entries.name: CHASE_MANUAL_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder where Chase CSV activity downloads or PDF statements are dropped, one subfolder per account. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo, with one subfolder per account named for its type and last four digits, such as checking-1234 or card-5678.
In Chase online banking, download activity as CSV, or statements as PDF, into each account's folder.

entries.name: CLOVER_MERCHANT_ID
entries.description: The Clover merchant's 13-character ID. Not a secret, but it names the client's business. The connector checks that the token answers for this merchant before it reads anything.
howToGet: In the merchant's Clover dashboard, open Settings > View all settings, then Merchants under About Your Business, and copy the 13-character merchant ID.
It also appears in the dashboard's address, after /merchants/.

entries.name: CLOVER_REGION
entries.description: Which Clover API host the merchant is on: north_america (api.clover.com), europe (api.eu.clover.com), latin_america (api.la.clover.com) or sandbox (apisandbox.dev.clover.com). The connector calls no other host.
howToGet: Use the region the merchant's Clover account was opened in: North America (the US and Canada), Europe or Latin America.
Use sandbox only for a developer test merchant.

entries.name: CLOVER_APP_ID
entries.description: App ID of the KaratOS app in the Clover Developer Dashboard, which is the OAuth client_id for refreshing tokens. With CLOVER_APP_SECRET and CLOVER_REFRESH_TOKEN, the connector keeps its own expiring tokens current.
howToGet: In the Clover Developer Dashboard, open Your Apps, pick the app, then App Settings, and copy the App ID.

In Requested Permissions, tick only Read merchant, Read orders, Read payments, Read inventory and Read customers. No Write permissions: Clover offers no way to check them later, so this is where read-only starts.

entries.name: CLOVER_APP_SECRET
entries.description: App secret of the Clover app. The connector doesn't send it; it is the key the instance seals its stored refresh token with, so rotating it means reconnecting the merchant.
howToGet: On the app's App Settings page in the Clover Developer Dashboard, copy the App Secret straight into the host's secret store.
After rotating it, reconnect the merchant and set a new CLOVER_REFRESH_TOKEN, because the stored token can no longer be decrypted.

entries.name: CLOVER_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the merchant with Clover's v2 OAuth flow. Clover retires it on every refresh, so after the first sync the instance keeps the newest one encrypted in its database and this value only seeds it. Replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over from the stored one.
howToGet: Have the merchant install the KaratOS app, then exchange the authorization code at /oauth/v2/token on the merchant's regional host.
Copy the refresh_token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: CLOVER_API_TOKEN
entries.description: A merchant-specific API token, instead of the app sign-in, for one merchant (Clover documents these for test merchants). It doesn't expire; the connector only ever sends it with GET requests.
howToGet: In the merchant's Clover dashboard, open Settings > View all settings > API tokens and create a token.
Tick only the Read permissions for merchant, orders, payments, inventory and customers.
Copy it straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: CLOVER_WEBHOOK_AUTH_CODE
entries.description: The Clover app's webhook auth code, which Clover sends in X-Clover-Auth with every notification. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: In the Clover Developer Dashboard, open the app's App Settings > Webhooks, enter the webhook URL and verify it with the code Clover posts to it.
Copy the Clover Auth Code shown there straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: TYPEFORM_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: A Typeform personal access token for the account that owns the forms, used to read their definitions and responses.
howToGet: In Typeform, open Account > Personal tokens and generate a new token for KaratOS.
Give it only the forms:read and responses:read scopes. Typeform can't report a token's scopes, so nothing checks this later; the connector only sends GET requests either way.
Copy the token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: TYPEFORM_FORM_IDS
entries.description: The Typeform forms to read, by id, separated by commas. Not a secret.
howToGet: A form's id is the last part of its link: in https://example.typeform.com/to/u6nXL7 it is u6nXL7.

entries.name: TYPEFORM_API_HOST
entries.description: Which Typeform host the account keeps its responses on: api.typeform.com, api.eu.typeform.com or api.typeform.eu for the newer EU data center. api.typeform.com when empty; the sync stops with the right host named if it is wrong.
howToGet: Leave empty unless the account is on an EU data center; the first sync says which host to set if it is.

entries.name: TYPEFORM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: The secret set on a Typeform webhook, which signs each delivery (Typeform-Signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: Generated by npm run secrets:setup. Set the same value as the secret on each form's webhook in Typeform.

entries.name: FORMS_MAPPING_PROFILE
entries.description: How the forms are built: generic, or the path to a form mapping profile JSON kept in the client's private instance repo.
howToGet: Leave as generic when the forms use the question names in docs/integrations.md.
Otherwise write a profile for the client's forms in their private instance repo and put its path here.

entries.name: EDI_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder where the business's VAN or SFTP mailbox keeps its X12 files, both what partners sent and copies of what was sent to them. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.
Have the VAN or SFTP client copy every inbound and outbound X12 file (.edi, .x12, .txt or .dat) into it. Leave the mailbox itself as it is: KaratOS reads copies and never sends.

entries.name: GIA_API_URL
entries.description: The Report Results API address GIA gives when the API key is issued. Only https addresses on a gia.edu host are accepted, so the key can't be sent anywhere else.
howToGet: In the GIA Client Portal, apply for Report Results API access under Useful links.
Copy the API address from the signup confirmation.

entries.name: GIA_API_KEY
entries.description: A GIA Report Results API key. It reads reports only. Each plan can have several keys; give KaratOS its own so it can be revoked alone.
howToGet: In the GIA Client Portal, open GET API KEYS and create a key for KaratOS.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: GIA_REPORT_NUMBERS_FILE
entries.description: A text or CSV file of the GIA report numbers to look up, one per line in the first column, such as the certificate numbers on the business's stones. Blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Export the certificate number column for GIA-graded stones from the POS or inventory system.
Save it outside any git repo and put its path here. Add new numbers to the end; each is looked up once.

entries.name: GIA_MAX_LOOKUPS_PER_SYNC
entries.description: The most new report numbers one sync looks up. Lookups of reports the business didn't submit cost money on a pay-as-you-go plan, so this caps what one sync can spend. Defaults to 100.
howToGet: Leave unset for 100.
Raise it for the first import of a large inventory, after checking the plan's remaining lookups.

entries.name: GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the mailbox with the gmail.metadata scope. Google doesn't rotate it, so this value keeps working until the owner revokes access, changes their password, leaves it unused for six months, or (for an External consent screen still in Testing) seven days pass. The instance keeps a sealed copy in its database in case Google ever returns a new one; replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over.
howToGet: Have the mailbox owner connect the mailbox to the instance's OAuth client with access_type=offline, prompt=consent and exactly the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.metadata, for example through Google's OAuth 2.0 Playground using the client's own credentials (add https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground as an authorized redirect URI).
The connector stops if the token holds any other Gmail scope (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.labels, gmail.send, gmail.compose or https://mail.google.com/), so don't add them.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: GMAIL_USER
entries.description: Which mailbox to read: me (the account that connected, the default) or that account's address. One mailbox per instance. Not a secret, but it names the mailbox.
howToGet: Leave empty for me. Each further mailbox needs its own instance.

entries.name: GMAIL_LABEL_NAMES
entries.description: Whether user label names are kept: keep (the default) keeps names such as Bridal or Vendors, leaving out any with an @ or four digits in a row; drop keeps label ids only, for a mailbox whose labels are named after customers.
howToGet: Leave empty for keep. Use drop if labels in the mailbox carry customers' names.

entries.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_ROOT_FOLDER_ID
entries.description: The Drive folder the business shares with Brain A. Everything below it is read as metadata (names, types, folders, sizes, edit times); file contents are never downloaded.
howToGet: Open the folder in Google Drive and copy the id after /folders/ in the address bar.
The Google account that connects must be able to open the folder. A whole shared drive can be read instead, or as well, with GOOGLE_DRIVE_SHARED_DRIVE_IDS.

entries.name: GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the business's Google account with the three read-only scopes drive.metadata.readonly, spreadsheets.readonly and calendar.events.readonly. It uses the same OAuth client as Gmail but is a separate connection, because each connector stops if its token holds any scope beyond its own. Google doesn't rotate it; the instance keeps a sealed copy in case Google ever returns a new one.
howToGet: Have the account owner connect to the instance's OAuth client with access_type=offline, prompt=consent and exactly these scopes: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.metadata.readonly, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.readonly (spreadsheets.readonly only if GOOGLE_SHEETS_RANGES is set, calendar.events.readonly only if calendars are read). Google's OAuth 2.0 Playground with the client's own credentials works (add https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground as an authorized redirect URI).

The connector stops if the token holds anything else, such as drive.readonly (which can download files), drive, drive.file, spreadsheets, calendar, calendar.readonly, calendar.events or a Gmail scope, so don't add them.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_SHARED_DRIVE_IDS
entries.description: Shared drives to read whole, besides the shared folder: comma-separated shared drive ids. Each is walked like a folder and gets its own change feed.
howToGet: Leave empty to read only the shared folder.
Open the shared drive in Google Drive and copy the id after /folders/ in the address bar.

entries.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_FILE_NAMES
entries.description: Whether file and folder names are kept: keep (the default) or drop, for a business whose files are named after customers. With drop, only ids, types, folders, sizes and times are kept.
howToGet: Leave empty for keep. Use drop if file names carry customers' names.

entries.name: GOOGLE_SHEETS_RANGES
entries.description: The only spreadsheet ranges whose values are read: comma-separated spreadsheetId/Sheet!A1:F500 entries. Sheet names may hold letters, digits, spaces, _ . and -, quoted when they hold a space. Nothing else is read from any spreadsheet. List ranges without customers' personal details; a cell that is only an email address is kept as a correspondent reference.
howToGet: Leave empty to read no spreadsheet values.
Open the spreadsheet and copy the id between /d/ and /edit in the address bar, then add / and the range in A1 notation, as Google Sheets shows it.

entries.name: GOOGLE_CALENDAR_IDS
entries.description: Which calendars' appointments are read: primary (the default, the connected account's own calendar), none, or comma-separated calendar ids such as a shared appointments calendar's address. Not a secret, but it names the calendars.
howToGet: Leave empty for primary. Use none to read no calendars.
For another calendar, open its settings in Google Calendar and copy the Calendar ID under Integrate calendar.

entries.name: GOOGLE_PUSH_CHANNEL_TOKEN
entries.description: The token Drive and Calendar push channels are opened with and echo back in X-Goog-Channel-Token, which is how the instance tells a genuine notification from a forged one (Google doesn't sign them). Only used once push channels are turned on through the write gate.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.
After rotating it, open new push channels: notifications on the old ones are refused.

entries.name: HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: Access token of the HubSpot private app the connector reads contacts, companies, deals, tickets and engagements with. The connector asks HubSpot which scopes it holds before every sync and refuses one that could change data.
howToGet: A HubSpot super admin opens Settings > Integrations > Private Apps (Development > Legacy apps in newer accounts) and creates a private app named KaratOS.

On its Scopes tab, select exactly these read scopes: crm.objects.contacts.read, crm.objects.companies.read, crm.objects.deals.read and crm.objects.tickets.read. Contacts read also covers calls, emails, meetings, notes and tasks.
Don't add any write scope or the older tickets scope, which can change tickets: the connector refuses a token that holds one.
Create the app and copy its access token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: HUBSPOT_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: Client secret of the HubSpot private app, which signs its webhook deliveries (X-HubSpot-Signature-v3). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: On the private app's Auth tab in HubSpot, copy the Client secret straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: IDEX_API_KEY
entries.description: The API key IDEX issues for the Onsite feed. It names the account and isn't secret on its own.
howToGet: Ask the IDEX account manager to turn on the Onsite feed add-on for the trading subscription.
Set the feed's filters and markups on IDEX, then copy the API key IDEX issues for it.

entries.name: IDEX_API_SECRET
entries.description: The API secret that comes with that key. KaratOS sends it only to IDEX's Onsite feed addresses.
howToGet: Copy the API secret IDEX issues with the key.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: IDEX_FEEDS
entries.description: Which Onsite feeds to read: natural, lab_grown, or both comma-separated. Defaults to natural; the lab-grown feed is a separate IDEX add-on.
howToGet: Leave unset for the natural feed only.
Add lab_grown once IDEX has turned on the lab-grown add-on.

entries.name: IDEX_MAX_STONES
entries.description: The most stones one feed may hold before the sync stops and asks for narrower filters on IDEX. Defaults to 50000.
howToGet: Leave unset for 50000.
Raise it only if the feed's filters on IDEX are meant to cover more stones.

entries.name: POS_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder on the owner's machine or the instance's volume where point-of-sale CSV exports are dropped. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.
Export items, stock on hand, customers and sales from the POS as CSV into it. Each export can be a new file; a file that changes is read again.

entries.name: POS_MAPPING_PROFILE
entries.description: Which columns the POS exports use: generic, or the path to a mapping profile JSON kept in the client's private instance repo.
howToGet: Leave as generic when the exports use the column names in docs/integrations.md.
Otherwise write a profile for the client's POS in their private instance repo and put its path here.

entries.name: KLAVIYO_PRIVATE_API_KEY
entries.description: A Klaviyo private API key with read-only scopes, for profiles, lists, segments, campaigns, flows and their figures. Klaviyo can't be asked which scopes a key holds, so the connector can't check it; it only sends its listed reads whatever the key allows.
howToGet: In Klaviyo, open Settings > Account > API keys (an Owner, Admin or Manager can) and choose Create Private API Key. Name it KaratOS.

Choose Custom Key and give Read Access to Profiles, Lists, Segments, Campaigns, Flows and Metrics, and No Access to everything else. Never pick Full Access Key, and never reuse an old key: keys made before scopes existed have full access.
Copy the key (pk_...) straight into the host's secret store. Klaviyo shows it once.

entries.name: KLAVIYO_CONVERSION_METRIC_ID
entries.description: Optional. The id of the metric the campaign and flow reports count conversions and revenue by. Empty means the metric named Placed Order, which Klaviyo's own reports use.
howToGet: Leave empty unless the store records orders under another metric. To find one, open Analytics > Metrics in Klaviyo, open the metric and copy the id from the page address.

entries.name: KLAVIYO_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: Secret of a Klaviyo system webhook, which signs each delivery (Klaviyo-Signature over the body and Klaviyo-Timestamp). Only Advanced KDP customers and Klaviyo app partners can create webhooks; the scheduled sync works without them.
howToGet: Only if the account has webhooks: create the webhook with the Webhooks API, choosing your own random secret_key, and put the same value in the host's secret store.

entries.name: META_APP_ID
entries.description: Meta app for Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp.
howToGet: At developers.facebook.com, create a Business app and copy its App ID.

entries.name: META_APP_SECRET
entries.description: Secret for the Meta app.
howToGet: In the Meta app, go to Settings > Basic and copy the App Secret.

entries.name: WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: System-user token for the WhatsApp Business API.
howToGet: In Meta Business Settings, create a system user, assign the WhatsApp app, and generate a permanent token.

entries.name: WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID
entries.description: The WhatsApp business phone number's id (not the number itself).
howToGet: In the Meta app, go to WhatsApp > API Setup and copy the Phone number ID.

entries.name: METALS_API_KEY
entries.description: Access key for Metals-API spot prices. It can only read prices; Metals-API has nothing to write to.
howToGet: Sign up at metals-api.com. The free plan is enough to start; a paid plan updates more often and allows more requests a month.
Copy the API key from the dashboard.

entries.name: METALS_API_HISTORY_DAYS
entries.description: Days of daily closing prices the first import reads, from 1 to 1825. Every 30 days costs four requests, one per metal.
howToGet: Leave empty for a year (52 requests). Check the plan's monthly request allowance before asking for more.

entries.name: MONDAY_API_TOKEN
entries.description: monday.com API token the connector reads boards, items and updates with. A monday app's OAuth token granted only boards:read and updates:read is the safer choice, since monday.com then refuses every change. A personal API token carries everything its user can do and can't be limited; the connector still only sends its own read queries.
howToGet: Safer: in monday.com's Developer Center, create an app, give its OAuth settings only the boards:read and updates:read scopes, install it on the account and copy the access token from the OAuth flow. Set MONDAY_OAUTH_SCOPES to the scopes it was granted.
Simpler: as a user who can see the boards to sync, click your avatar > Developers > API token and copy it. It can change anything that user can, so use one with no more access than needed.
Copy the token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: MONDAY_OAUTH_SCOPES
entries.description: For a monday app's OAuth token, the scopes it was granted, as the token response's scope field lists them. The connector refuses to run if any of them could change data. Leave it unset for a personal API token.
howToGet: Copy the scope field from the response that gave the OAuth access token. It should read boards:read updates:read.

entries.name: MONDAY_ALLOWED_COLUMNS
entries.description: Columns whose display text the connector may keep although their type can hold personal data (text, long text, email, phone, location, files, links), as comma-separated board:column pairs. Unset keeps none of them; status, date, numbers, checkbox, dropdown, timeline and people columns are always kept.
howToGet: Only allow a column the business agrees to share, such as a ring size or an order number kept in a text column, never one with customer names or contact details.
The board id is the number in the board's address; the column id shows under the column's menu when Developer mode is on in monday.com's monday labs.

entries.name: MONDAY_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET
entries.description: The monday app's Signing Secret, which signs the JWT on webhook deliveries for webhooks the app creates. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: In monday.com's Developer Center, open the app, then Basic Information, and copy the Signing Secret straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: PLAID_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: Client ID of the KaratOS team on the Plaid Dashboard. It is the same in sandbox and production; the secret decides which.
howToGet: On dashboard.plaid.com, open Developers > Keys.
Copy the client_id straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: PLAID_SECRET
entries.description: The Plaid secret for the environment in PLAID_ENVIRONMENT: the Sandbox secret for sandbox, the Production secret for production. It is sent in the PLAID-SECRET header, never in a request body.
howToGet: On dashboard.plaid.com, open Developers > Keys and copy the secret for the environment the instance uses straight into the host's secret store.
After rotating it on the Dashboard, update this value before the old secret is deleted.

entries.name: PLAID_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: The access token of the business's linked bank (a Plaid Item). It does not expire, and it reads that bank's accounts and transactions, so keep it as carefully as the bank login.
howToGet: Have the business link its bank through Plaid Link with the transactions product only, then exchange the public token Link returns with /item/public_token/exchange.
Copy the access token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
If a sync fails with ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED, have the business sign in again through Link's update mode; the token stays the same.

entries.name: PLAID_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which Plaid API the Item is on: sandbox for Plaid's test banks, production for a real one. There is no default, so a sandbox setting can't reach a client's bank by accident and the other way round.
howToGet: Use sandbox with the Sandbox secret and production with the Production secret.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: Client ID of the KaratOS app on the Intuit Developer portal, used with the client secret to refresh QuickBooks access tokens.
howToGet: On developer.intuit.com, open the app under My Hub > App dashboard, then Keys and credentials. Use the Development keys with the sandbox company and the Production keys with the client's company.
Copy the Client ID straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: Client secret of the Intuit app. It refreshes access tokens and is the key the instance encrypts its stored refresh token with, so rotating it means reconnecting QuickBooks.
howToGet: In the same Keys and credentials page, copy the Client Secret straight into the host's secret store.
After rotating it, reconnect the company and set a new QUICKBOOKS_REFRESH_TOKEN, because the stored token can no longer be decrypted.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID
entries.description: The QuickBooks company's realm ID, shown as Company ID. Not a secret, but it names the client's books.
howToGet: The realmId comes back with the authorization code when the company is connected.
In QuickBooks it is under Settings > Account and settings > Billing and subscription, as Company ID.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the company. Intuit rotates it about daily, so after the first sync the instance keeps the newest one encrypted in its database and this value only seeds it. Replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over from the stored one.
howToGet: Have a QuickBooks admin connect the company to the KaratOS app with the com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting scope, for example through Intuit's OAuth 2.0 Playground with the app's own keys.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
Intuit has no read-only accounting scope; the connector only sends GET requests, and its writes stay behind the write gate.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which QuickBooks API the company is on: sandbox for an Intuit developer sandbox company, production for a real one. There is no default, so a sandbox setting can't reach a client's books by accident and the other way round.
howToGet: Use sandbox with Development keys and production with Production keys.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_WEBHOOK_VERIFIER_TOKEN
entries.description: Verifier token for QuickBooks webhooks, which signs each delivery (intuit-signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: On the app's Webhooks page on developer.intuit.com, copy the Verifier Token straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: RAPNET_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: The client ID of a Rapaport Trade API access key made for KaratOS. It names the key and isn't secret on its own.
howToGet: The primary account holder signs in to Rapaport Trade and opens Settings, Privacy, API Access.
Create an access key for KaratOS with the price list, and copy its client ID.

entries.name: RAPNET_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: The client secret of that access key. KaratOS sends it only to Rapaport's token service, and uses the token to read the price list.
howToGet: Copy the client secret shown when the access key is created.
Put it straight into the instance's Railway variables. Never send it by chat or email.

entries.name: SHOPIFY_SHOP_DOMAIN
entries.description: The store's myshopify.com domain.
howToGet: In Shopify admin, go to Settings > Domains and copy the myshopify.com domain.

entries.name: SHOPIFY_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: Client ID of the store's Dev Dashboard app. With SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET, the connector requests a 24-hour Admin API token and renews it itself.
howToGet: Sign in to the Shopify Dev Dashboard as the store owner, so the app and the store share an organization.

Create an app, and in its version grant only these Admin API scopes: read_orders, read_all_orders, read_products, read_customers and read_inventory. Without read_all_orders Shopify returns only the last 60 days of orders. No write scopes.
Release the version, install the app on the store, then copy the Client ID from the app's Settings.

entries.name: SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: Client secret of the store's Dev Dashboard app, used only to request Admin API tokens. It also signs webhooks, so set SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET to the same value.
howToGet: In the Shopify Dev Dashboard, open the app's Settings and copy the Client secret straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: SHOPIFY_ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: Permanent Admin API token of an older custom app made in the store admin. Use it instead of SHOPIFY_CLIENT_ID and SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET only when the store already has such an app.
howToGet: Shopify stopped letting merchants create these apps on 2026-01-01; new stores use SHOPIFY_CLIENT_ID and SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET.

For an existing app, in Shopify admin go to Settings > Apps and sales channels > Develop apps, check it holds only read_orders, read_all_orders, read_products, read_customers and read_inventory, and copy its Admin API access token.

entries.name: SHOPIFY_API_VERSION
entries.description: Shopify Admin API version the connector pins, e.g. 2026-07. Defaults to the version the connector was tested with.
howToGet: Leave empty to use the tested default. Shopify supports each quarterly version for 12 months; move up when the vendor docs watch reports a change.

entries.name: SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: The Shopify app's client secret, which signs webhook deliveries (X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256). Only needed when webhooks are turned on.
howToGet: For a Dev Dashboard app, use the same value as SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET.
For an older admin-made app, open its API credentials under Settings > Apps and sales channels > Develop apps and copy the API secret key.

entries.name: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
entries.description: The Bot User OAuth Token of the business's own Slack app, installed with read scopes only. The connector reads messages and threads in the channels the bot is invited to, and stops if the token holds any other scope, such as chat:write.
howToGet: At api.slack.com/apps, create a new app from scratch in the business's own workspace and don't distribute it, so it keeps Slack's internal-app limits.

Under OAuth & Permissions > Bot Token Scopes, add exactly channels:read and channels:history, and groups:read and groups:history if private channels should be read. Add nothing else: no chat:write, users:read or files:read.
Install the app to the workspace, copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-) straight into the host's secret store, then invite the bot (/invite @app-name) to each channel it should read.

entries.name: SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET
entries.description: Verifies Events API deliveries Slack sends to this instance (X-Slack-Signature). Optional: the instance doesn't take Slack webhooks yet, and the scheduled sync reads the same messages.
howToGet: At api.slack.com/apps, open the app > Basic Information > App Credentials, and copy the Signing Secret straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: SLACK_TEXT_CHANNELS
entries.description: Which channels keep their message text: none (the default) keeps who posted, when and where but no text; all keeps text from every channel the bot is in; or a comma-separated list of channel ids. Kept text has email addresses, phone numbers, other numbers of seven or more digits, link paths and people's names taken out.
howToGet: Leave empty for none. To keep text, open each channel in Slack, click its name and copy the Channel ID at the bottom of the About tab, then list the ids separated by commas.

entries.name: SLACK_APP_DISTRIBUTION
entries.description: How the Slack app is distributed, which sets how fast history can be read: internal (the default), an app made in the business's own workspace, may read about 50 pages a minute; non_marketplace, an app installed from outside that isn't in the Slack Marketplace, may read 1 page of 15 messages a minute since May 2025.
howToGet: Leave empty for internal. Set non_marketplace only if the app was installed from another workspace and isn't listed in the Slack Marketplace.

entries.name: SQUARE_APPLICATION_ID
entries.description: Application ID of the KaratOS app in the Square Developer Console. With SQUARE_APPLICATION_SECRET and SQUARE_REFRESH_TOKEN, the connector refreshes its access token and asks for the read scopes only each time. Not a secret.
howToGet: Sign in to developer.squareup.com, open the app (or create one for KaratOS), and copy the Application ID from its Credentials page. Use the Sandbox tab for testing and Production for the store.

entries.name: SQUARE_APPLICATION_SECRET
entries.description: The Square app's application secret, used only to refresh the OAuth access token.
howToGet: On the app's OAuth page in the Square Developer Console, show the Application secret and copy it straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: SQUARE_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from the seller authorizing the KaratOS app (the OAuth code flow). Square keeps returning the same one, so it doesn't need saving after each refresh; revoking the app's access ends it.
howToGet: Have the seller authorize the app with exactly these scopes: MERCHANT_PROFILE_READ ITEMS_READ INVENTORY_READ CUSTOMERS_READ ORDERS_READ PAYMENTS_READ. No _WRITE scopes: the connector stops if the token holds any other scope.
Exchange the authorization code for tokens (ObtainToken with grant_type authorization_code) and copy the refresh_token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: SQUARE_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: Instead of the three OAuth settings above: an OAuth access token already limited to the read scopes. It lasts 30 days and is not refreshed. A personal access token from the Developer Console has full access, so the connector stops with one.
howToGet: Prefer SQUARE_APPLICATION_ID, SQUARE_APPLICATION_SECRET and SQUARE_REFRESH_TOKEN. Use this only for a short test with an OAuth token holding exactly MERCHANT_PROFILE_READ ITEMS_READ INVENTORY_READ CUSTOMERS_READ ORDERS_READ PAYMENTS_READ.

entries.name: SQUARE_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which Square host to read: production (connect.squareup.com) or sandbox (connect.squareupsandbox.com). production when empty.
howToGet: Leave empty for a live store. Set sandbox only for a Square developer sandbox seller.

entries.name: SQUARE_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY
entries.description: Signature key of the app's webhook subscription, which signs each delivery (x-square-hmacsha256-signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: In the Square Developer Console, open the app's Webhooks > Subscriptions, pick the subscription and copy its Signature key straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: SQUARE_WEBHOOK_URL
entries.description: The notification URL set on the webhook subscription, character for character. Square signs it together with the body, so a different URL fails every check.
howToGet: Copy the Notification URL from the same webhook subscription in the Square Developer Console.

entries.name: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
entries.description: Restricted Stripe key with read-only access. A full secret key (sk_) is rejected, because it can move money.
howToGet: In the Stripe dashboard, go to Developers > API keys and select Create restricted key.
Set Read on charges, refunds, disputes, payouts, balance and balance transactions, customers and events. Leave every other permission at None.
Copy the key, which starts rk_live_, straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: Verifies that webhooks really came from Stripe.
howToGet: In Stripe, go to Developers > Webhooks, add this instance's webhook URL with the charge, refund, dispute, payout and customer events, and copy its signing secret.

entries.name: STRIPE_API_VERSION
entries.description: Stripe API version the connector pins, e.g. 2026-09-30.endive. Defaults to the version the connector was tested with.
howToGet: Leave empty to use the tested default. Move up when the vendor docs watch reports a Stripe changelog change that the connector has been tested against.

entries.name: TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID
entries.description: The Twilio account whose message and call logs are read.
howToGet: Shown on the Twilio Console home page as Account SID (AC followed by 32 characters).

entries.name: TWILIO_API_KEY_SID
entries.description: SID of a restricted API key that can only read message and call logs. The account's Auth Token is never used: it can change anything on the account.
howToGet: In the Twilio Console, go to Account > API keys & tokens and create a Restricted key named KaratOS read-only.
Give it only the read permissions for Messaging messages and Voice calls, and no others.
Copy the key's SID (SK followed by 32 characters).

entries.name: TWILIO_API_KEY_SECRET
entries.description: Secret of the restricted API key.
howToGet: Shown once, when the restricted key is created. Put it straight into the password manager and the instance settings.

entries.name: TWILIO_CONTACT_KEY
entries.description: The instance's own key for turning customers' phone numbers into contact references (HMAC-SHA256), so texts and calls with the same person line up without the number being kept. Changing it gives every customer a new reference, so it is never rotated.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup. Keep a copy in the password manager.

entries.name: WATCHSEARCH_IMPORT_DIR
entries.description: Folder where WhatsApp chat exports from the store's dealer groups are saved, one .txt file per group, named after the group. Never inside a git repo.
howToGet: Create a folder outside any git repo.

In WhatsApp, open each dealer group, choose Export chat > Without media, and save the .txt file into the folder named after the group, such as Rolex Dealers HK.txt. On iPhone the export is a zip holding _chat.txt: unzip it and rename the file.
Export again whenever you want fresh offers; a newer export of the same group replaces the old file, and offers already read are recognized.

entries.name: WATCHSEARCH_DEALER_KEY
entries.description: The instance's own key for turning dealer names and numbers into dealer references (HMAC-SHA256), so offers from the same dealer line up without the name or number being kept. Changing it gives every dealer a new reference, so it is never rotated.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup. Keep a copy in the password manager: losing it means earlier offers no longer line up with new ones by dealer.

entries.name: WATCHSEARCH_DATE_ORDER
entries.description: How the phone that exports the chats writes dates: auto, dmy (22/10/2026) or mdy (10/22/2026). Auto works it out from each file.
howToGet: Leave as auto. Set dmy or mdy only when a sync says a file's dates could be read either way, which happens when every message in it is from the first 12 days of a month.

entries.name: WATCHSEARCH_UTC_OFFSET
entries.description: The exporting phone's offset from UTC, such as +08:00 or -05:00. Exports carry the phone's local times.
howToGet: Use the time zone of the phone that exports the chats. Leave it empty for UTC.

entries.name: WATCHSEARCH_CURRENCY
entries.description: The currency the store's groups mean when a dealer writes a bare price such as 14.5k. Without it, those prices are left out and only prices with a currency are kept.
howToGet: Set it when most of the store's groups trade in one currency, using its three-letter code (USD, EUR, HKD).

entries.name: WIX_APP_ID
entries.description: The App ID of the self-managed Wix app KaratOS reads the site through. An app, not an API key: Wix lets the connector read back an app's granted permissions, so it can stop if any Manage permission is present, and only apps receive webhooks.
howToGet: In the Wix app dashboard (manage.wix.com, Custom Apps), open the KaratOS app and go to Develop > OAuth.
Copy the App ID.

entries.name: WIX_APP_SECRET
entries.description: The app's secret key, used only to request four-hour access tokens for the site (OAuth client credentials). The app must hold read permissions only; the connector stops on any Manage or write permission.
howToGet: In the app's dashboard, go to Develop > OAuth and copy the App Secret Key straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: WIX_INSTANCE_ID
entries.description: The app's instance ID on the client's site: one per site the app is installed on. It names the site in each token request and keys the site's customer references.
howToGet: Install the app on the client's site; the site owner approves its read permissions.
Wix sends the instance ID with the app's App Instance Installed webhook; copy it from there, or from the app's installation details in its dashboard.

entries.name: WIX_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY
entries.description: The app's public key (PEM), which verifies each webhook: Wix signs every delivery as a JWT (RS256). Not secret. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it. An API key gets no webhooks.
howToGet: In the app's dashboard, go to Develop > Webhooks and choose Public Key.
Copy the whole key, from the BEGIN PUBLIC KEY line to the END PUBLIC KEY line.

entries.name: WOOCOMMERCE_STORE_URL
entries.description: The WooCommerce store's home address, https only, e.g. https://shop.example.com (or https://example.com/shop when WordPress lives in a folder). Every request goes here and nowhere else: the connector refuses http, IP addresses, ports, user names in the address and hostnames that resolve to private networks, and never follows a redirect.
howToGet: Open the store in a browser and copy the address it settles on, including https:// and www. if the store uses it, without /wp-admin or /wp-json.

entries.name: WOOCOMMERCE_CONSUMER_KEY
entries.description: Consumer key of a WooCommerce REST API key with Read permission. WooCommerce has no way to ask a key's permission without sending a write, so the connector can't check it; it sends GET requests only, and a Read key keeps the store safe even if that ever failed.
howToGet: In WordPress, open WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API and choose Add key.
Describe it as KaratOS, pick an administrator or shop manager as the user, and set Permissions to Read. Never Write or Read/Write.
Generate the key and copy the Consumer key (it starts ck_) straight into the host's secret store. WooCommerce shows it only once.

entries.name: WOOCOMMERCE_CONSUMER_SECRET
entries.description: Consumer secret of the same Read key. Sent only in the Authorization header over https, never in an address.
howToGet: Copy the Consumer secret (it starts cs_) shown with the key straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: WOOCOMMERCE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: The secret set on the store's webhooks, which signs each delivery (X-WC-Webhook-Signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup. Paste it as the Secret of each webhook under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Webhooks. Letters and digits only: WooCommerce decodes HTML entities in the secret before signing.

entries.name: XERO_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: Client ID of the KaratOS app in Xero's developer portal, used with the client secret to refresh Xero access tokens.
howToGet: On developer.xero.com, open My Apps, pick the app (a Web app), then Configuration.
Copy the Client id straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: XERO_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: Client secret of the Xero app. It refreshes access tokens and is the key the instance encrypts its stored refresh token with, so rotating it means reconnecting Xero.
howToGet: On the app's Configuration page, generate a client secret and copy it straight into the host's secret store. Xero shows it once.
After rotating it, reconnect the organisation and set a new XERO_REFRESH_TOKEN, because the stored token can no longer be decrypted.

entries.name: XERO_TENANT_ID
entries.description: The Xero organisation's tenant ID. Not a secret, but it names the client's books.
howToGet: After the organisation is connected, call GET https://api.xero.com/connections with the access token and copy the tenantId of the organisation (tenantType ORGANISATION).
A connection can cover several organisations; each one needs its own instance.

entries.name: XERO_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the organisation. Xero retires it on every refresh and drops it after 60 days unused, so after the first sync the instance keeps the newest one encrypted in its database and this value only seeds it. Replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over from the stored one.
howToGet: Have a Xero adviser or standard user connect the organisation to the KaratOS app with exactly these scopes: offline_access accounting.settings.read accounting.contacts.read accounting.invoices.read accounting.payments.read accounting.banktransactions.read accounting.manualjournals.read.
The connector rejects a connection holding any scope beyond read-only, so don't add others.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: XERO_WEBHOOK_KEY
entries.description: Webhook signing key for Xero webhooks, which signs each delivery (x-xero-signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: On the app's Webhooks page on developer.xero.com, copy the Webhooks key straight into the host's secret store.
